Max Engling

Republican candidate for Secretary of State, Indiana · Open seat

Former senior advisor to U.S. Sen. Jim Banks; former congressional staffer

Max Engling is the Republican nominee for Indiana Secretary of State and lives in Cicero, in Hamilton County. He was working as a senior advisor to U.S. Sen. Jim Banks when he entered the race on May 20, 2026. On June 20, 2026, he won the nomination on the second ballot at the Indiana Republican convention, where Knox County Clerk David Shelton finished second and incumbent Diego Morales finished third.

Where Engling stands

Voter eligibility / citizenship verification
Says only U.S. citizens should vote in Indiana elections. Proposes verifying voter eligibility and sending evidence of possible violations to prosecutors, and says he would work with Attorney General Todd Rokita to enforce election laws.
Closed primaries
Supports closed primaries, which he says would protect the integrity of the Republican nomination process.
Election transparency
Proposes a "Transparency Portal" where citizens could report possible election issues directly.
Business filing fraud
Proposes screening business filings for shell companies that register identical LLCs, which he says are used to defraud customers, avoid regulation and employ unsafe truck drivers.
Business regulation
Proposes cutting regulations he describes as onerous for small businesses and streamlining the office's business services.

Background

  • Republican nominee for Indiana Secretary of State, chosen at the state GOP convention on June 20, 2026
  • Senior advisor to U.S. Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.) until the 2026 campaign
  • Ran in the 2024 Republican primary for Indiana's 5th Congressional District and received nearly 10% of the vote
  • Worked at Beck's Hybrids on an agricultural education initiative
  • Staff member on the U.S. House Administration Committee, which oversees federal election administration; later a senior staff member in House leadership
  • Worked for a small business in Indiana after college
  • B.A., IUPUI; M.A. in National Defense and Strategic Planning (as a civilian), U.S. Naval War College
  • Lives in Cicero, Indiana; married with four children
